title: ASDA: Automated Skill Distillation and Adaptation for Financial Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2603.16112v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Adapting large language models (LLMs) to specialized financial reasoning typically requires expensive fine-tuning that produces model-locked expertise. Training-free alternatives have emerged, yet our experiments show that leading methods (GEPA and ACE) achieve only marginal gains on the FAMMA financial reasoning benchmark, exposing the limits of unstructured text optimization for complex, multi-step domain reasoning. We introduce Automated Skill Distillation and Adaptation (ASDA), a framework that automatically generates structured skill artifacts through iterative error-corrective learning without modifying model weights. A teacher model analyzes a student model's failures on financial reasoning tasks, clusters errors by subfield and error type, and synthesizes skill files containing reasoning procedures, code templates, and worked examples, which are dynamically injected during inference. translated_title: ASDA：面向金融推理的自动化技能蒸馏与适配
translated_abstract: 将大型语言模型（LLM）适配到专业金融推理任务通常需要昂贵的微调，而这会产生被锁定在特定模型上的专业知识。无需训练的替代方案虽已出现，但我们的实验表明，现有的领先方法（GEPA和ACE）在FAMMA金融推理基准上仅能取得微小的提升，这暴露了非结构化文本优化在应对复杂多步领域推理时的局限性。我们提出了自动化技能蒸馏与适配框架（ASDA），该框架通过迭代式的错误纠正学习自动生成结构化的技能工件，且无需修改模型权重。具体而言，教师模型会分析学生模型在金融推理任务中的失败案例，按子领域和错误类型对错误进行聚类，并合成包含推理流程、代码模板和详细示例的技能文件，这些文件在推理过程中被动态注入。在FAMMA基准上的评估显示，ASDA实现了高达……（摘要此处截断）
tldr: ASDA是一个无需微调的框架，通过教师模型分析学生模型的失败案例并自动生成包含推理流程、代码模板和示例的结构化技能文件，在推理时动态注入，从而显著提升LLM在金融推理任务上的表现，突破了现有免训练方法的局限。
en_tdlr: ASDA is a training-free framework that improves LLM financial reasoning by having a teacher model analyze student failures and automatically generate structured skill files (reasoning procedures, code templates, and worked examples) dynamically injected at inference, overcoming the limitations of existing training-free methods.
